reviewed_by: Claude review of batched chat tool calls
reason: The chat routing loop accepted exactly one tool call per provider response: OpenRouter batches were truncated to the first call and every other shape failed the turn with "provider must return exactly one sequential tool call" (live failure err_6c33d2be, 2026-09-19). A routing response may now carry several calls; Core validates the whole batch first, then executes it one call at a time, in order, so each call keeps its own durable step, budget, approval and event pair. The routing request stops disabling provider parallelism, and a required routing step that comes back with no call now answers from the results already gathered instead of failing. tests/v3/test_chat_tool_loop.py covers the batch contract end to end (order, steps, replay, finish_response inside a batch, mid-batch approval pause, mid-batch budget exhaustion, duplicate ids, empty response); tests/v3/test_provider_contracts.py pins the wire contract for a batched request on the Chat Completions and Anthropic adapters; tests/v3/test_tool_catalog.py and tests/v3/test_chat_subagents.py are the other suites that drive this loop, including the tool_catalog.call unwrapping that moved into the new batch validator.
exclusions: No frontend or native change: the loop still emits one tool_started/tool_completed pair per call, in order, so the transcript is unchanged and no ui/src file is touched. No Playwright area is selected. The only catalogued journey that drives a real model through this loop is provider-live-openrouter-gui, which skips in CI because no workflow provides OPENROUTER_API_KEY; selecting it would spend a real-Core job on a skip. That coverage was taken locally instead: a Core built from this branch, with a live OpenRouter profile on deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp, answered a three-file read with one batched routing response and three durable steps 35 ms apart, where the same prompt on origin/main took three routing round trips. The mission/specialist loop in agent_tooling.py keeps its own one-call-per-step contract and is not changed here.
